items.definition:
lack of experience, wisdom, or judgment
Her naivety made her vulnerable to scams.

elaborate display or ceremony
The royal wedding was full of pomp and pageantry.

a five-pointed star
The magician drew a pentagram on the floor.

thick viscous substance secreted by the mucous membranes
He coughed up some phlegm.

a person who owns or has something
The true possessor of the treasure was unknown.

the action or process of deciding the relative importance or urgency of a thing or things
Effective prioritization is key to managing tasks.

a person who is excessively concerned about sexual propriety
Some people consider him a prude because of his strict views.

a type of sleeve extending in one piece to the collar
She wore a sweater with raglan sleeves.

a large quantity of paper (usually 500 sheets) or a large amount of something
He bought a ream of paper for the printer.

the action of directing something to a new or different place or purpose
The website implemented a redirection to the new page.

a device that puts things in a specific order
The musician used a sequencer to program the drum beats.

the process of becoming an expert in a particular area
His specialisation is in artificial intelligence.

a member of a specialized shock troop; a fictional soldier from Star Wars
The child dressed up as a stormtrooper for Halloween.

a cut of meat from the loin
We had a delicious beef tenderloin for dinner.

land covered with timber-producing trees
The company owns vast tracts of timberland.

a male cat
Our neighbor's tomcat often visits our garden.

a burrowing marsupial native to Australia
The wombat is known for its powerful claws.

the practice of regularly staying away from work or school without good reason
The company is trying to reduce absenteeism among its employees.

a covered outdoor platform for a band to play on
The concert was held at the bandstand in the park.

a mixture of gases produced by the breakdown of organic matter, used as fuel
The farm uses biogas to generate electricity.

the study of living organisms
She is pursuing a career in bioscience research.

A highly intelligent person.
The new intern is a real brainiac; she solved the problem in minutes.

A line in a newspaper or magazine article giving the name of the writer.
Her name appeared in the byline of the front-page story.

A popular garden plant of the daisy family, with brightly colored ornamental flowers.
She arranged a beautiful bouquet of chrysanthemums for the table.

The action of making something narrower, or the state of being made narrower.
The snake's constriction tightened around its prey.

An attempt to prevent the public from discovering information about a serious crime or mistake.
The government was accused of a coverup regarding the scandal.

a cloud forming a rounded mass with a flat base, characteristic of fair weather
We saw fluffy cumulus clouds in the sky.

an athletic contest comprising ten different events
The athlete trained hard for the decathlon.

two games played on the same day between the same two teams
The baseball team played a doubleheader on Saturday.

the system in a vehicle that connects the transmission to the drive axles
The mechanic repaired the car's drivetrain.

the quality of being suitable for paid work
Good communication skills improve your employability.

a style of painting, music, or drama in which the artist or writer seeks to express emotional experience rather than external reality
German Expressionism was a significant art movement.

an outgoing, socially confident person
She is a natural extrovert and loves meeting new people.

something imagined or invented
The monster was a figment of his imagination.

a small mark or spot
There was a tiny fleck of paint on the window.

the opposite or less obvious aspect of something
On the flip side, the new policy could also bring benefits.

software that is available free of charge
Many useful applications are available as freeware.

a long narrow trench made in the ground by a plow
The farmer plowed deep furrows in the field.

a storehouse for threshed grain
The village relied on its granary to store the harvest.

a US dollar bill
He pulled a few greenbacks from his wallet.

the passing on of physical or mental characteristics genetically from one generation to another
Eye color is determined by heredity.

the basic form of a verb, typically preceded by 'to'
The infinitive form of 'run' is 'to run'.

a block of steel, gold, silver, or other metal, typically oblong in shape
They found a large gold ingot in the shipwreck.

an explosive mine laid on or just under the surface of the ground
The soldiers had to clear the area of landmines.

a game in which players vault over each other's bent backs
The children played a game of leapfrog in the park.

a program that combines object files into an executable program
The software development process involves a compiler and a linker.

skill in music
Her musicianship was evident in every note she played.

the ability to understand and work with numbers
Basic numeracy skills are essential for everyday life.

a theater or concert hall
The ancient Odeon was used for musical performances.

a type of bet where winnings from one bet are staked on the next
The gambler placed a parlay on three different races.

the action of designing or producing something to meet someone's individual requirements
The website offers a high degree of personalization for its users.

a meaningless word used in magic tricks (often in 'hocus pocus')
The magician said 'hocus pocus' before making the rabbit disappear.

a ghost or other supernatural being that makes its presence known by causing noise and disturbance
They suspected a poltergeist was responsible for the strange noises in the house.

the art or technique of making prints, especially as a fine art
She studied printmaking at art school.

a type of music characterized by a syncopated melodic line and regularly accented accompaniment
Scott Joplin was a famous composer of ragtime music.

steel reinforcing bar used in concrete
The concrete foundation was strengthened with rebar.

the quality of being distant or remote
The remoteness of the island made it a peaceful retreat.

a variety of white wine grape, or the dry white wine made from it
She ordered a glass of crisp Riesling with her meal.

Japanese rice wine
Would you like some warm saki with your sushi?

a substance or device used to seal something
We applied a concrete sealer to the garage floor.

a loose, lightweight overgarment worn to protect the wearer's clothes
The artist wore a paint-splattered smock.

a style of Caribbean music originating in Trinidad and Tobago
We danced to lively soca music at the carnival.

the minor component in a solution, dissolved in the solvent
Sugar is the solute when dissolved in water.

a person who is left-handed, especially in sports
The boxer was a powerful southpaw.
